# HP-6 (#400): generated bytecode is never published and never counts as a local edit

Base: `origin/epic/honest-pins` 433f1090ab6c (HP-0 merged).

## Local signal: `run.py honest-pins`, node `honest.record-d`

expected_effect: record shape (d) red -> green. **Observed: red -> green.**

| run | record-d | assertions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline (HP-0, `baseline/2026-11-07-1b52427/honest-pins.json`) | FAILED | `shape_bytecode_not_published` red; control `control_real_edit_is_published` green |
| this branch, sweep 20261107-185503, run 20261107-185542 (`sweep-honest-pins-green.json`, `record-d-green.envelope.json`) | PASSED | all six green, including the two new sync-half assertions and their control |

Node log line on this branch:

```
publish rc=0 moved=true; remote tree=SKILL.md,skill-manager.toml,tool.py; editPublished=true;
sync(bytecode only) rc=0 refused=false reached=true bytecodeKept=true;
sync(bytecode+edit) rc=7 refused=true editKept=true; consumersSetup=true
```

The other eight honest-pins shape nodes stay red on their `shape_*` assertions, as in the
baseline: they are other tickets' slices (HP-2..HP-8, HP-10). Their control arms are unchanged.

The node now also covers the sync half (HP-0 noted it measured only the publish half).
Two consumer homes install from the remote before the publish, and each gets untracked
`__pycache__` bytecode. The consumer with only bytecode syncs to the published commit and
keeps the bytecode (shape). The consumer with bytecode and a real `SKILL.md` edit is still
refused with "extra local changes" and keeps its edit (control).

**The graph was not re-run red for the new sync-half assertions.** A node-only resume with
the production change reverted was started, then cancelled after about 70 minutes waiting
on the shared graph lock. The red-before evidence for the sync half is the unit case below.
The red-before evidence for the publish half is the HP-0 baseline.

## Unit: `GeneratedContentTest`

Red before the fix: production `GitOps.commitAll` and `DereferencedStoreLinks` reverted,
`GeneratedContent` kept so the test compiles. 4 of 6 cases fail
(`unit-GeneratedContentTest-red-before-fix.txt`): commitAll commits
`__pycache__/tool.cpython-312.pyc` and `stray.pyo`, and bytecode alone counts as an
authored change. With the fix: 6/6.

Full `jbang RunTests.java`: **ALL PASSED** (second run). The first run reported
`FAILURES: 1` with no `[FAIL]` line or failing suite count anywhere in its log. That log was
damaged: JsonContractTest's stdout re-latch overwrote a stretch of the redirected file
(39 cases declared, 8 lines visible), so the failing case cannot be named. The rerun piped
through `cat` so nothing can seek the file, and it was clean. This is recorded as a likely
flake (compare DEF-HP0-001); it is not attributed to this change.
